note.p: She appears in the 1796 list for 1799. Although the DNB has her fl. between 1763-1783, there is no reason to think that coming off the stage was the end of her. She is likely to have been born in 1746 to William and Sarah Cheny/Cheney (and was 17 on her marriage if the record for St Giles in the Fields for 4 October 1764 is correct (her mother testifying to her as a minor) and with her father deceased. We know that she had several children by William Gardener (m. 1763 possibly 1764), from whom she became estranged, and who predeceased her in 1790. Nothing was head from her after 1795, but she may well have met Godwin in 1799, and he may also have met her daughters in 1796 - and King was well-known as a place for those in debt (and that was something of which Mrs Gardner had considerable experience). If she is the Mrs Gardner of 1828, then she has reached a considerable age (82). And it may be her or a daughter in 1831.
Given the uncertainties, we have coded only the mes Gardners of 1795, the Mrs Gardner of the 1796 list (for 1799), the corresponding plural Gardners of 1799 and 1800s, and the Mrs Gardner of 1828.
